The Art of
Investment
Misery

A Practical Guide to Financial Self-Sabotage

Veteran investor Norm Conley exposes the common pitfalls that sabotage even the smartest investors. With humor, insight, and sharp analysis, the book traces how emotion, short-term thinking, and flawed assumptions turn portfolios into cautionary tales.

Purchase on Amazon Watch Trailer

Promotional Video

A sharper look at bad investor habits.

The trailer carries the book’s wink and warning: plenty of investors know what they should do, then quietly do the opposite. This preview belongs beside the core pitch, close enough to turn curiosity into a purchase.

Why This Book Matters

Are you leaving money on the table?

Most investing books promise easy riches. This one does the opposite, which is exactly why it works. By naming the mistakes clearly, you learn how to stop making them.

Emotional Decision-Making

Fear and greed are the silent portfolio killers. Gut reactions consistently undermine even the most rational strategies.

Short-Sighted Strategies

Chasing returns, market timing, and trend-following feel smart in the moment and cost dearly over the long run.

Flawed Assumptions

Conventional wisdom and popular tactics can paradoxically lead to mediocre, even disastrous, results.

The Compounding Trap

Understand the magic of compounding and why most investors sabotage it before it ever has a chance to work.

About the Author

Norm Conley

CEO & CIO · JAG Capital Management · St. Louis, MO

Norm Conley is a veteran investor with over three decades of experience in financial markets. As Chief Executive Officer and Chief Investment Officer of JAG Capital Management, he has led strategic initiatives and managed equity and fixed-income strategies since 1999.

A University of Notre Dame alumnus and former naval officer, Norm began his investment career at Merrill Lynch before earning his MBA in Finance from Washington University’s Olin School of Business. Known for blending rigorous market insight with wit and candor, he brings a rare combination of expertise and relatability to personal finance.
